messages:
Mira: FYI I'm seeing a repeated leader election + apiserver latency bump during GPU pool attach windows in eu-west1. Controller-manager reconciles spike and we lose 10-20% throughput for a few mins. Dashboard: https://go/redwood/d/ctlplane-eu-west1

Ben: Could be our attach-controller doing a big fanout at once. Any correlation with attach QPS or conntrack?

Mira: Attach QPS spikes right when new instances come up. conntrack high but not saturated. kube-apiserver logs show a lot of deadlines and: 
```
E0318 10:12:03.456 apiserver.go:234] Unexpected EOF reading from client
I0318 10:12:04.782 lease_controller.go:145] failed to renew lease: context deadline exceeded
```

Chao: That lease renewal line smells like apiserver->etcd latency. Have we seen etcd leader stepdowns at the same time?

Mira: Etcd leader stays mostly, but commit latency spikes to ~200-300ms. NVMe IO looks noisy on the leader node.

Nora: Is this limited to the GPU-onboard subnet / zone? Any NAT gateway or SNAT exhaustion?

Sam: I checked NAT metrics — ephemeral port usage increases but not full. However egress paths for that pool go through a smaller set of NATs while onboards are warming caches.

Ben: Two failure modes we should consider: 1) heavy attach fanout causing apiserver conn backlog -> etctd IO amplification, 2) kernel TCP buffers + socket churn on leader causing stalls.

Mira: Agreed. Options: throttle attach-controller concurrency, stagger onboarding, or increase apiserver and etcd headroom (IO/CPU). Also we could route onboarding traffic to a warm standby NAT pool.

ops-oncall: Created alert ticket IDS-1329, pinned runbook: "cp-degrade-during-gpu-onboard". Deploy-bot scheduled a canary to test reduced concurrency.

deploy-bot: Started canary with attach-controller concurrency=8 (was 32) in eu-west1 at 10:35 UTC.

Nora: Quick mitigation: add a short startup jitter to the onboarding job (random 0-90s) and bump etcd journal async write config on the leader to lower tail latency. Both safe?

Chao: Jitter is low-risk. Changing etcd fsync knobs is riskier — needs careful testing, could impact durability. Prefer increasing IO reserve on leader hosts (burst iops/queue depth) for now.

Sam: Cost note — increasing NVMe IOPS or larger instances will add ~15-25% monthly to that zone's infra bill if sustained. If we can fix with smarter throttling we avoid that.

Mira: I can flip the attach-controller concurrency to 6 and enable jitter for the next 2-hour window. Will monitor apiserver p95 and etcd commit_latency.

Ben: Also add a short-lived ingress rule to spread egress across two NAT pools for onboarding traffic only (30m). That should reduce hot NAT saturation.

Mira: Doing both now. Will post metrics in 15.

Sam: If this recurs we should formalize a GPU onboarding rate limiter in the provisioner with a cost-aware default.

Nora: Agreed. Filing RFC action item for rate limiter + warm NAT pool design.

Mira: Update: after changes p95 apiserver dropped from ~480ms -> ~110ms, etcd commit p95 from 320ms -> 90ms. Looks like the combined mitigation helped. :thumbsup:

Chao: Nice! Can we capture the experiment as a short playbook for next onboarding wave?

Mira: Yep — I'll add notes to runbook and attach graphs.

ops-oncall: Closing IDS-1329 as mitigated, attaching timeline and links.

Ben: Follow-up: schedule a cost/benefit review for increasing host io vs implementing a provisioner-side rate limiter. Assign to infra-costs board.

Mira: Assigned. Thanks all.
